ety.text: Uncertain. From a non-Slavic language. First attested in 1810 in Kamchatka. Later attested through the whole Northern Siberia and in Transbaikalia. Also attested in European Russia around Vologda, upper Pinega and Solvychegodsk. Anikin points out that the existance of the term in European part of Russia suggests a Uralic North-European origin, rather than a Siberian language. Kabinina makes further suggestion that сендуха may be from some obsolete Finnic word, with suffix related to Karelian -ndeh (compare Finnish -nne).
